questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The fraudsters hoodwinked us and took away all our valuables.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

The fraudsters hoodwinked us and took away all our valuables.
questions.solution: The correct answer is: Deceived. The word "hoodwinked" means to trick or deceive someone. The meanings of the other words are: Coerced: Forced someone to do something; Threatened: Expressed an intention to harm; Misguided: Led by faulty judgment.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Irrevocable
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Irrevocable
questions.solution: 'Irrevocable' means not able to be changed or reversed. Eg. The decision was irrevocable. 'Irreversible' means not able to be undone or reversed. Eg. The damage caused by the earthquake was irreversible, leaving the town forever changed.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. The young fellow was innocent and without guile .
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The young fellow was innocent and without guile.
questions.solution: 'Guile' means cunning or deceitful behavior. Example: He used guile to get ahead in his career. 'Deceit' is the action or practice of deceiving someone by concealing or misrepresenting the truth. Example sentence: She was caught in her deceit when her lies were uncovered.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence. Roads in villages during rainy seasons become muddy.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence.

Roads in villages during rainy seasons become muddy.
questions.solution: The correct answer is: Filthy. The word "muddy" refers to something covered in or full of mud, which implies being dirty. The meanings of the other words are: Fuzzy: frizzy or blurred; Blurred: unclear or out of focus; Unsoiled: clean or not dirty.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. The efforts of the doctors came to a futile end with the death of the patient.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The efforts of the doctors came to a futile end with the death of the patient.
questions.solution: The correct answer is: Fruitless. The word "Futile" refers to something that is incapable of producing any useful result or is pointless. The meanings of the other words are: Enriching: Improving the quality or value of something; Startling: Very surprising or astonishing; Terrifying: Causing extreme fear.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. Marcella seemed morose and downcast when she refused to have dinner.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

Marcella seemed morose and downcast when she refused to have dinner.
questions.solution: 'Morose' describes a person who is sullen, sad, and not cheerful. Example: The team was in a morose mood after losing the championship game. The word 'gloomy' means dark, dim, or depressing.  Example: Sarah's face looked gloomy and sad when she heard the bad news about her grandfather.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Distant
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Distant
questions.solution: The correct answer is: Faraway. The word "Distant" refers to something that is far away in space or time. The meanings of the other words are: Farsighted: Having foresight or seeing distant objects clearly; Futuristic: Relating to the future; Forward: Moving toward the front.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym for the underlined word in the given sentence. You also worked with another eccentric genius.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym for the underlined word in the given sentence.

You also worked with another eccentric genius.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Peculiar'.

Key Points

  • The most appropriate synonym of the underlined word 'eccentric' is 'peculiar'.
  • Eccentric: Unconventional and slightly strange; odd or peculiar. (असामान्य)
    • Example: The eccentric old man who lived down the street had a habit of wearing a top hat and carrying a cane everywhere he went.
  • Peculiar: Unusual or unconventional; strange. (विचित्र)
    • Example: The old man down the street had a peculiar habit of talking to himself and wearing mismatched socks.
       

Correct Answer: Peculiar.

Additional Information

  • Let's look at the meaning of other options:
    • Middle: Being at an equal distance from the extremities of something; intermediate. (मध्यम)
    • Ecological: Relating to or concerned with the relation of living organisms to one another and to their physical surroundings. (पारिस्थितिक)
    • Elusive: Difficult to find, catch, or achieve; evasive. (दुर्लभ)

questions.question: Select the option that is similar in meaning to the underlined word. He declined the offer to join the Board of Directors.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that is similar in meaning to the underlined word.

He declined the offer to join the Board of Directors.
questions.solution: 'Declined' is to refuse or reject something, often politely. Eg. She declined the invitation to the party because she had other plans. 'Rejected' is to refuse to accept, to deny approval to something or someone. Eg. The committee rejected his proposal for a new project.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Chide
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Chide
questions.solution: The correct answer is: Scold. The word "Chide" means to rebuke or express disapproval of someone, typically for their behavior. The meanings of the other words are: Prevent: To stop something from happening; Rescue: To save from danger; Follow: To go or come after.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. Isn't knowledge supposed to make life sweeter and happier?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Isn't knowledge supposed to make life sweeter and happier?
questions.solution: The correct answer is: Wisdom. The word "Knowledge" refers to the facts, information, and skills acquired through experience or education, which is most closely synonymous with "Wisdom" in this context. The meanings of the other words are: Curriculum: The subjects comprising a course of study; Profession: A paid occupation; Superiority: The state of being higher in rank or quality.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Zealous
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Zealous
questions.solution: In the given question, the word "zealous" means having great energy or enthusiasm. We are required to select the synonym of the given word. Now, among the given options the word "enthusiastic" is the correct synonym as it means having intense interest or enjoyment.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. She had an ability to persuade others.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.

She had an ability to persuade others.
questions.solution: In the given sentence, the word "persuade" means to convince someone to do or believe something. Now, among the given options, the word "impress" can substitute it as it also means to make someone feel admiration or respect.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Feeble
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Feeble
questions.solution: In the given question, the word "feeble" means someone/ something very delicate or frail. We are required to select the synonym of the given word. Now, among the given options the word "useless" is the correct synonym as it means something having very little energy or strength.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Insidious
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Insidious
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Harmful."

Key Points
  •  Let us understand the meaning of the given and the marked words:
    • "Insidious" means something that is harmful or dangerous but is not easily noticeable.
      • ​Example: The insidious virus spread silently among the population, causing widespread illness.
      • Synonyms of insidious include treacherous, deceitful, and sneaky.
    • "Harmful" means something likely to be damaging; injurious.
      • Example: Fast food is harmful to your health.
  • Thus, it is clear that the word "harmful" is the synonym of the word "insidious."

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Additional Information
  • Option 1, Protected, means to be kept safe or defended from harm.
  • Option 2, Secure, means to be safe from danger or threat.
  • Option 3, Safe, means to be free from harm or danger.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Matching
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Matching
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Resembling."

Key Points
  •  Let us understand the meaning of the given and the marked words:
  • "Matching" means to have the same colour/pattern or qualities as something else.
    • Example: He wore a matching shirt with the jacket.
  • "Resembling" means to be similar or bear a likeness to something/someone.
    • Example: The new statue resembles the old one in every way.
  • From the above explanation, it is clear that the word "resembling" is the synonym of the word "matching."

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Additional Information
  • "Appointing" means to assign a job or position to someone.
  • "Distinguishing" means to recognize or differentiate something/someone from others.
  • "Adoring" means to love and admire someone/something deeply.

Hinglish 

  • Appointing: नियुक्ति करना
    • Example: उसने अपने बेटे को कंपनी का नए CEO के रूप में नियुक्त कर दिया।
    • He appointed his son as the new CEO of the company.
  • Distinguishing: अंतर निर्धारित करना
    • Example: उसने दोनों उत्पादों के बीच मायने रखने वाले अंतर को निर्धारित कर दिया।
    • He distinguished the significant differences between the two products.
  • Adoring: पूजना, बहुत प्यार करना
    • Example: वह अपनी मां को बहुत प्यार करता है।
    • He adores his mother a lot.
  • Resembling: समानता
    • Example: उसकी आँखें उसकी माँ की आँखों के समान होती हैं।
    • His eyes resemble his mother's eyes.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. He was offered a _____ (moderate) price for his bungalow.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.

He was offered a _____ (moderate) price for his bungalow.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4 (reasonable).

KEY POINTS:
- Synonym of "moderate" is "reasonable".
- "Reasonable" means fair and sensible.
- Example: He asked for a reasonable price for his car.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:
- Option 1 (sustainable) means able to be maintained at a certain rate or level.
- Option 2 (considerable) means large or significant.
- Option 3 (respectable) means deserving of respect or admiration.
- Option 5 (blank) means there is no option given to choose from.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The efforts will be in vain if we do not submit the project report on time.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

The efforts will be in vain if we do not submit the project report on time.
questions.solution: In the given question, the word "vain" means something ineffective or futile. We are required to select the synonym of the given word. Now, among the given options the word "useless" is the correct synonym as it means something having no value or purpose.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Natwar was a fraudster who always tried to fooling others.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Natwar was a fraudster who always tried to fooling others.
questions.solution: In the given question, the word that can substitute the underlined word "fooling" means to trick someone is "deceive" which means to trick or mislead someone. Thus, among the given options the correct substitute is "deceive."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Consent
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Consent
questions.solution: In the given question, the word "assent" means to approve or accept something. We are required to select the synonym of the given word. Now, among the given options the word "consent" is the correct synonym as it means to give approval to something.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The burglar was very vigilant , so he avoided the security perfectly as they didn’t find any proof.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

The burglar was very vigilant, so he avoided the security perfectly as they didn’t find any proof.
questions.solution: Vigilant means being watchful and alert, while cautious means being careful and avoiding risks. Hence, 'cautious' is the most appropriate synonym for 'vigilant'. Example- "The security guard remained vigilant all night." and "She proceeded cautiously on the slippery path." Thus, option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given word. Harangue
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given word.

Harangue
questions.solution: The term "harangue" refers to "a forceful and lengthy speech that is usually aggressive and critical in nature." Example- "The opposition leader used the platform to harangue the ruling party's decisions." The word is frequently used negatively, implying that the speaker is being overly critical or harsh in their approach. The term is often applied to political speeches or public addresses intended to convince or influence an audience.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The company was engaged in spurious trade practices.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

The company was engaged in spurious trade practices.
questions.solution: "Spurious" means fake, false or not genuine. "Fraudulent" means deceitful or dishonest. The synonym for the underlined word is "Fraudulent" as it conveys the same meaning as "Spurious". Example- "The company's promise of overnight riches was both fraudulent and spurious."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. He became verbose after a few drinks.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

He became verbose after a few drinks.
questions.solution: The word "verbose" means using more words than necessary, or being excessively wordy. The synonym for "verbose" is "talkative," which means liking to talk a lot or speaking easily and often. Example- "During the long car ride, her talkative nature kept us entertained."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The government's utilitarian stance was appreciated by all.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

The government's utilitarian stance was appreciated by all.
questions.solution: 'Utilitarian' refers to something that is beneficial or practical. Functional, pragmatic, and effective are all synonyms for "utilitarian." 'Useful' is the word that best describes the highlighted word in this situation. As a result, selection 3 is the right response.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The committee wanted us to explain this in detail.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

The committee wanted us to explain this in detail.
questions.solution: Elaborate means to explain in detail, which is the same as the underlined word in the sentence. The word is often used in academic or professional contexts. Example- "He asked her to elaborate on the details of her plan."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Consequence
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Consequence
questions.solution: Consequence refers to the outcome or impact of a behaviour. Outcome refers to the outcome of a process or activity. Both terms have equivalent meanings and are typically interchangeable.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Certain
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Certain
questions.solution: In the given question, the word "certain" means to be completely sure about something and having no doubts. Now, among the given options, the word "definite" also has the same meaning as the word "certain." Thus, the word "definite" is synonymous to the word "certain."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. He is very _______ (Eager) to join the Air Force.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.

He is very _______ (Eager) to join the Air Force.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option no. (2) "keen".  Key Points

  • "Eager" means enthusiastic, excited, or willing to do something.(इक्छुक)
  •  "Keen" is a synonym of "eager", meaning having a strong desire or interest in something.(चाहत रखने वाला)
  •  Grammatically, "keen" is an adjective that can describe a person or their feelings.
  • As both the words eager and keen are similar in meaning.

Therefore,the correct answer is option no.(2)

 Additional Information

  • Option 1, "irksome", means annoying or irritating.(कष्टप्रद) 
  • Option 3, "dubious", means uncertain or doubtful.(संदिग्ध) 
  • Option 4, "unconcerned", means not caring or showing interest in something.(बेखबर)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The benevolent gesture of the rich merchant was appreciated by all.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

The benevolent gesture of the rich merchant was appreciated by all.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option no.(1) 'Generous'.  Key Points

  • The word 'benevolent' (परोपकारी) means kind and generous. - The synonym of 'benevolent' is 'generous'.
  • 'Generous' (उदार) means showing a readiness to give more of something, especially money, than is strictly necessary or expected 
    • Example: The rich merchant's gesture was appreciated by all because he was kind and generous.
  • As both the words benevolent and generous are similar in meaning.
  • Therefore,the correct answer is option no.(1)

 Additional Information

  • Option 2 'Sombre' means dark or dull in color or tone; gloomy. (गंभीर, उदास)
  • Option 3 'Numb' means deprived of the power of sensation; deadened. (सुन्न, असंवेदनशील)
  • Option 4 'Sober' means not affected by alcohol; not drunk. (संयमी, होश में)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Tedious
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Tedious
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option no. (1) 'Tiresome'.Key Points

  • The word 'Tedious' means too long, slow, or dull; tiresome or monotonous.(थकाऊ)
    • Example:-  The journey was too much tedious.
  • The word 'Tiresome' means causing one to feel bored or annoyed. (थकाने वाला)
    • Example:- Weeding is a tiresome but essential job.
As both the words Tiresome and Tedious are similar in meaning.

Therefore,the correct answer is option no.(1)Additional Information

  •  Other options are:
    • Wholesome- conducive to or suggestive of good health and physical well-being.(लाभदायक)

    • Threescore- being three times twenty;sixty.(साठ)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Incredible
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Incredible
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Unbelievable.

Key Points

  • The word 'Incredible' is an adjective, meaning impossible to believe, or extremely good, great or large (Hindi meaning: अविश्वसनीय).
    • For example: "The magician performed some truly incredible tricks."
  • The correct synonym is 'Unbelievable', which in this context means not able to be believed; unlikely to be true (Hindi meaning: अविश्वसनीय).
    • For example: "He made an unbelievable catch in the baseball game."

Therefore, the correct answer is "Unbelievable".

Additional Information

  • Realistic: This word describes something that is sensible and reasonably like real life (Hindi meaning: यथार्थवादी). 
  • Unachievable: It refers to something that cannot be achieved or completed successfully (Hindi meaning: असाध्य). 
  • Reasonable: 'Reasonable' indicates something that is fair, practical, and sensible (Hindi meaning: योग्य).

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Adamant
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Adamant
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Stubborn'.
 
Key Points
  • The word 'Adamant' means refusing to be persuaded or to change one's mind. It represents inflexibility or unwavering determination. (अटल).
    • Example: Despite the convincing arguments from his colleagues, he remained adamant on his decision.
  • The word 'Stubborn' is the synonym of adamant. Stubborn means having or showing dogged determination not to change one's attitude or position on something, especially in spite of good arguments or reasons to do so. (ज़िद्दी).
    • Example: The stubborn child refused to eat his vegetables, despite his parents' plea.
Therefore, the correct answer is- 'Option 3'.
 
Additional Information
  • 'Flexible': This means capable of bending easily without breaking or willing to change or compromise. (लचीला)
  • 'Soft': This typically means easy to mold, cut, compress, or fold; not hard or firm to the touch or having a pleasing quality involving a subtle effect or contrast rather than sharp definition. (मुलायम )
  • 'Adaptable': Adaptability implies that someone or something is capable of adjusting to new conditions or situations. (अनुकूलनीय)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Abhijeet feels extremely tired after working all day long.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Abhijeet feels extremely tired after working all day long.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. exhausted.

Key Points

  • The word tired means feeling in need of rest or sleep; weary. (थका हुआ)
    • Example: After the long hike, everyone was very tired and ready to relax.
  • Exhausted means completely used up or used out of energy; drained of energy or effectiveness. (शिथिल)
    • Example: By the end of the marathon, all the runners were completely exhausted.
  • Hence, we can infer that someone who is very tired can also be described as being exhausted.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. exhausted.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Depressed (उदास): In a state of general unhappiness or despondency.
    • Example: She felt depressed after the loss of her pet.
  • Sleepy (नींद आना): Needing or ready for sleep.
    • Example: After the big meal, he felt very sleepy.
  • Bare (नंगा): Not clothed or covered.
    • Example: The bare branches of the trees looked eerie in the moonlight.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Authentic
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Authentic
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Genuine".

Key Points

  • Authentic means genuine or real. 
    • Example: The authentic painting was easily distinguishable from the imitation pieces.
  • Genuine means truly what something is said to be; authentic.

Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 1".

Additional Information

  • Option 2, false, means not true or genuine. 
  • Option 3, doubtful, means uncertain or questionable. 
  • Option 4, corrupt, means dishonest or immoral.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. It was due to treacherous leaders that he decided to leave the party.

The synonym of "treacherous" is "disloyal."

questions.question: Direction: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The investment scheme had been a scam all along.

Direction: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

The investment scheme had been a scam all along.

questions.question: Direction: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'. Many noticeable people were present at the function.

In this case, "notable" is a better fit because it implies that the people present were important or noteworthy.

questions.question: Direction: Select the option that is similar in meaning to the given word. Hapless
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Select the option that is similar in meaning to the given word.

Hapless
questions.solution: "Hapless" means unlucky or unfortunate. Example: The hapless flood victims were stranded on rooftops for ten days. The word "fortunate" means lucky. Example: It was fortunate that he was at home when you phoned. Therefore, the option that is similar in meaning to the given word is "Unfortunate."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Immerse
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Immerse
questions.solution: In the given question, the word "immerse" means to get fully involved into something. This itself explains how the word "involve" is the synonym of the word "immerse."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Absorbed
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Absorbed
questions.solution: In the given question the word "absorbed" means fully immersed, engrossed in something. We are asked to select an synonym of the given word. Now, among the given options, the word "soaked" in option 2 also means fully immersed or absorbed in something. Thus, "soaked" is the synonym of the word "absorbed."

questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Arthur has some strange ideas, but on this occasion, I am inclined to agree with him.
questions.solution: In the given sentence, the word "inclined" means to want to behave in a particular way. On the other hand, among the given options, the word "tended" also means to have an inclination to do something. Thus, it becomes clear that the word "tended" is the synonym of the word "inclination."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the following sentence. During the wedding ceremony, the bride seemed even quieter and more diffident than usual.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the following sentence.

During the wedding ceremony, the bride seemed even quieter and more diffident than usual.

options.text: Giving a false or misleading impression
options.html: Giving a false or misleading impression

options.text: Shy due to lack of confidence.
options.html: Shy due to lack of confidence.

questions.solution: Diffident refers to a lack of confidence or shyness. It is an adjective that describes a person's personality or behaviour. Example- He is very diffident and needs encouragement. As a result, the most accurate definition of 'diffident' is "shy due to lack of confidence." As a result, option 4 is the right answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Fierce
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Fierce
